what_happened: In job ywyz, the user corrected Athena's first reading of a retry request. The reading did not match what the user meant. The user restated three things. (1) The code and prompt change from the last attempt stays as it was. (2) For criterion 6, the older CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry saying the producer must run the full suite (D95) gets a short note that the new decision supersedes it, and it is not deleted. (3) The full test suite runs at most once. The correction came before the work went on. The event does not say what the first reading wrote, so this account of the gap is inferred from what the user restated.
cause: Athena builds the reading of a follow-up or retry request from the request text. It does not take in the earlier attempt's result, meaning which parts to keep and which are still open. It also does not check each criterion against the earlier decisions and changelog entries it touches. The reading therefore had no stated end state for the kept work, no rule for how to handle the superseded D95 entry (annotate, not delete), and no bound on test runs. Only the user's correction supplied these.
prevention: When a request is a retry or follow-up of an earlier job, the reading stage must be given that job's final diff summary and verifier findings. The reading must then open with a section listing what is kept unchanged, what is still to do, and the end state. For any criterion that supersedes an earlier decision or changelog entry, the reading must state the handling as annotate-and-keep, since the changelog is append-only. A reading missing the kept/open section for a retry is sent back before dispatch.
proposed_request: Retry job ywyz. Keep the code and prompt change exactly as the last attempt made it; do not redo or alter it. For criterion 6, add a short note to the older CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry that says the producer must run the full suite (the D95 entry), stating that the new decision supersedes it. Do not delete or rewrite that entry. Run the full test suite at most once. Confirm that the diff against the last attempt touches only the CHANGELOG note.
